agents.task: Test business logic flaws and privilege escalation on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: 1) Shopping cart/order manipulation (pricing, quantities, discounts), 2) Race conditions in order placement and payment, 3) Role-based access control (RBAC) bypass attempts to access admin endpoints, 4) Workflow abuse (order without payment, multiple checkouts), 5) Data manipulation in requests. Create test accounts with different roles and attempt escalation to admin. Document all successful bypasses with working PoCs.

Test for CSRF and unauthorized admin panel access on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: 1) Admin panel endpoints (/admin, /management, /console, /debug) for unauthorized access, 2) CSRF protection on state-changing operations (POST/PUT/DELETE), 3) Token/cookie handling in admin functions, 4) Privilege escalation to admin role. Attempt to access admin panels with and without authentication. Document all successful bypasses and unauthorized accesses with working PoCs.

Test file upload and remote code execution vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on /api/FileUpload endpoint. Test: 1) Upload of executable files (php, jsp, sh), 2) Bypass techniques (extension manipulation, magic bytes, polyglots), 3) Path traversal in upload parameters, 4) Access to uploaded files. Attempt to achieve RCE by uploading and executing code. Document all findings with working PoCs if successful.

Test for IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: 1) /api/Users/:id endpoint with numeric IDs, 2) User-specific resources (addresses, payment cards, orders), 3) Parameter tampering on user-scoped operations. Create test accounts and attempt to access other users' data by modifying ID parameters. Document all findings including unauthorized data access attempts. Spawn validation agents for confirmed IDORs.

Test authentication and JWT vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Test: 1) JWT token structure and signing (alg: none, algorithm confusion, weak secrets), 2) Login/register/forgot-password endpoints for bypasses, 3) Token expiration and refresh mechanisms, 4) Claim manipulation for privilege escalation. Build PoCs for any successful bypasses. Also test for account enumeration, brute force resistance, and credential stuffing on auth endpoints. Document all findings.

Test for path traversal and local file inclusion vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: 1) /ftp endpoint for directory traversal, 2) File upload path parameters, 3) Static asset paths (/assets), 4) Any file-serving endpoints. Attempt to access files outside intended directories (/etc/passwd, application config, etc.). Document all successful file access attempts with working PoCs.

Perform comprehensive reconnaissance on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Map the complete attack surface including: all endpoints, parameters, user roles, authentication mechanisms, technology stack, and any APIs or hidden paths. Use tools like httpx, katana, ffuf, and JavaScript analysis. Document all findings in detailed notes so the root agent can understand the application structure and delegate vulnerability testing. Do NOT perform any vulnerability testing - focus only on discovery and mapping.

Test for SQL injection vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: 1) Public endpoints (/api/Products, /api/Challenges, /api/SearchResults), 2) Search/filter parameters, 3) User input fields. Use both union-based and blind/time-based techniques. Target endpoints that accept query parameters. Build PoCs demonstrating data extraction if successful. Document all findings including request/response pairs. Spawn a validation agent if a promising SQLi candidate is found.

Independently validate the SQL injection vulnerability in /rest/products/search?q parameter at http://host.docker.internal:3100. The SQL Injection Specialist (ce90631e) has reported a high-severity boolean-based blind SQLi vulnerability. Your task: 1) Reproduce the finding with fresh requests (don't rely on the specialist's work), 2) Confirm the boolean-based blind pattern with alternative payloads, 3) Verify data extraction capability, 4) Test edge cases and alternative injection vectors, 5) Build a working standalone PoC, 6) Document findings thoroughly. Upon completion, use agent_finish to report validation results.

Test for Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: 1) Reflected XSS in search, product names, user input fields, 2) Stored XSS in reviews, comments, user profiles, 3) DOM-based XSS in Angular application, 4) CSP bypass techniques. Test both reflected and stored variants with payloads designed to execute in the Angular context. Use agent-browser for dynamic validation of XSS payload execution. Document all findings with working PoCs.

entries.evidence: Boolean-based SQL injection confirmed. Payload ' OR '1'='1 returns all 46 products instead of baseline 3. Payload ' AND '1'='2 returns 0 products. Response count differentiation proves injection.

Testing shows OR/AND payloads do not differentiate response counts in expected ways. Parameter appears to use case-insensitive LIKE matching on product names. While single/double quotes show differential responses, this is due to character matching in product names, not SQL injection. The q parameter behaves differently from /rest/products/search - no boolean-based injection pattern detected.

Tested with OR/AND injection payloads. No response differentiation observed. All injection attempts return 0 items, same as normal searches with non-existent values. Parameter does not appear to be injectable.

Endpoint exists but returns 500 errors due to Angular router intercepting the route. File upload surface confirmed via feedback comment indicating PDF-only file type restrictions on complaint uploads. Actual working upload mechanism not fully mapped - endpoint routing issue prevents direct testing. /uploads/ directory exists and is accessible (HTTP 200) but contains no uploaded files to exploit.

Tested boolean-based blind SQLi with payloads `q=juice' AND '1'='1` and `q=juice' AND '1'='2`. Both returned identical 30-byte responses with empty data arrays. No response length differential detected. Time-based SLEEP(2) payload returned 500 error with no delay. The reported vulnerability claim could not be validated. Input appears to be parameterized or escaped at the database layer, preventing SQL injection through the search parameter.
